evals.prompt: Review this proposed repository setup: CLAUDE.md copies the root AGENTS.md, while the same worktree and testing rules are copied into every project. Propose a durable layout for the guidance and explain what should be the source of truth.
evals.expected_output: Collapse the copies so each rule is written once: worktree and testing behavior that holds across every project belongs to the user-level guidance file, while conventions that only make sense inside one repository stay in that repository's `AGENTS.md`. `CLAUDE.md` stops being a maintained duplicate of the root `AGENTS.md` and instead becomes a relative symlink to it, so Claude loads the same bytes. The proposed layout is justified by where each rule is actually read, not by which file the request happened to name.
assertions: The response recommends one source of truth instead of copied AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md content.
The response separates user-level rules from repository-specific rules.
The response recommends a relative CLAUDE.md symlink when appropriate.

evals.prompt: This is a self-contained hypothetical setup: all facts and ownership evidence are supplied below, and no current-repository facts should be inferred. A coding agent repeatedly publishes pull-request bodies with literal escaped newlines. The existing user-level owner is `~/.agents/AGENTS.md`, which contains this exact relevant prevention rule: `Write multi-line GitHub issue, pull request, and comment bodies to a temporary Markdown file with a single-quoted heredoc, then submit them with --body-file. After creating or editing repository-facing GitHub text, read it back with gh pr view, gh issue view, or equivalent JSON output.` The repository's `AGENTS.md` has no copy of this prevention. I think the prevention rule belongs in this repository's AGENTS.md. Assess that placement and propose the next action.
evals.expected_output: Do not add the rule to the repository `AGENTS.md`. The supplied evidence shows `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` already owns the heredoc plus `--body-file` and read-back prevention, and that file is loaded in sessions for this repository, so a repository-level restatement would create a second owner for behavior that is already covered. The next action is to leave the repository file untouched and, if anything is lacking, sharpen the existing user-level rule; the placement decision follows the ownership evidence rather than the filename the user proposed.
assertions: The response does not blindly duplicate the requested rule in the repository AGENTS.md.
The response bases its target decision on scope and source-of-truth evidence rather than the filename in the request.
The response names `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` and its supplied prevention rule as the source of truth and uses that ownership as the reason not to add a repository duplicate.

evals.prompt: Simplify a long AGENTS.md by moving its detailed rules into skills. Describe the migration procedure and the validation needed before deleting the original sections.
evals.expected_output: Describe a procedure that starts by enumerating every atomic rule in the long `AGENTS.md` before any section is compressed or deleted, then gives each rule a named landing place — a specific existing skill, another guidance file, or a removal the user explicitly approved with a recorded reason. Build the index in the other direction too, from each rule back to every file that now states it, so no rule ends up with two owners except adapters that are deliberately recorded as such. Carry over examples wherever prose alone would not reproduce the behavior. Deletion of the original sections is gated on a static contract that fails when a mapped rule disappears or a duplicate lingers outside its owner; behavioral evals of the moved capability do not substitute for that check, and nothing unmapped or unapproved is removed.
assertions: The response inventories each atomic source rule and maps every rule to a destination or explicitly approved removal.
The response reverse-audits the destinations for duplicate rules and assigns each rule one authoritative owner unless a thin adapter is intentional.
The response preserves disambiguating examples instead of assuming prose or model capability is enough.
The response requires a static migration contract in addition to behavioral model evals.
The response does not permit unmapped or unapproved deletions.

evals.prompt: This is a self-contained hypothetical dotfiles repository; use only the supplied facts. The exact safety rule `Fetch without writing FETCH_HEAD before creating a task worktree.` appears in three canonical files: the repository root `AGENTS.md`, `home/shared/AGENTS.md`, and `home/shared/agents/gh-workflow-manager.md`. Applying the dotfiles renders `home/shared/AGENTS.md` to `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` and the custom-agent file to `~/.agents/agents/gh-workflow-manager.md`. External clones read only the repository root and never receive these rendered user files. The owner's ordinary development sessions read both the repository root and rendered `~/.agents/AGENTS.md`. The gh-workflow-manager always reads rendered `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` before its custom-agent file. No wrapper copies the rule, and these are the complete consumer paths. Audit the apparent duplication and recommend what to keep, remove, or replace with a thin reference.
evals.expected_output: Decide one consumer path at a time. The repository root `AGENTS.md` is the only guidance an external clone ever receives, so its copy of the fetch rule is load-bearing. The rendered `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` serves the owner's cross-repository sessions, and its overlap with the root copy is deliberate rather than accidental. The gh-workflow-manager file is the genuine redundancy, because that agent always loads the rendered user-level file first — remove its copy or reduce it to a pointer. Identical wording does not by itself prove redundancy and differing scope labels do not by themselves prove independent consumption, so the three copies do not get one blanket verdict.
assertions: The response maps each canonical source to its rendered path and actual readers, including which readers co-load higher-scope guidance.

The response keeps the repository-root rule for standalone external clones and the rendered user-level rule for cross-repository development, recognizing their intentional overlap for different consumer sets.
The response removes the custom-agent copy or replaces it with a minimal reference because gh-workflow-manager always co-loads the user-level owner.
The response does not classify all three copies as either required or redundant merely because their wording matches or their scope labels differ.
The response makes a separate ownership decision for each consumer path before recommending edits.

Route the preserved persistence-quality and skill-evaluation procedures into their named sections of the existing `shunk031-manage-agent-guidance` skill, leave skill-pool wiring with the README and exact gwq mechanics with gh-workflow-manager, and keep only concise repository-wide invariants in always-on guidance. The response keeps concise repository-wide invariants in root guidance and assigns specialized persistence and evaluation procedures to manage-agent-guidance.
The response keeps skill-pool wiring in its README owner and exact gwq mechanics in gh-workflow-manager instead of reintroducing them into always-on guidance.

evals.prompt: This is a fully self-contained hypothetical repository; all facts and ownership evidence are supplied below, so do not infer any current-repository facts. The repository's `AGENTS.md` contains an Incident Policy requirement with source ID `hypothetical-incident-policy-1` and exact source text `Bootstrap uses the configured runtime floor and preserves newer installations.` The adjacent comments in `config/runtime.toml` document the setting and its ownership but do not enforce behavior. Enforcement is supplied by the executable `scripts/bootstrap.sh` (which reads the configured floor, rejects unsupported versions, and preserves newer installations), `tests/bootstrap.bats` (which checks rejection and preservation of newer installations), the schema `schemas/runtime.json`, and `.github/workflows/bootstrap.yml` (which runs those checks on relevant changes). The supplied evidence is complete: the incident prose adds no human or agent judgment, and omission would not change behavior. The user asks whether to move the Incident Policy into a new skill, but has not yet approved deletion. Audit necessity before assigning a destination, preserve the machine-enforced owners, recommend the smallest durable action, and provide the proposed static migration record and approval gate.
evals.expected_output: Test necessity before picking any destination: the configured floor is read and enforced by `scripts/bootstrap.sh`, exercised by `tests/bootstrap.bats`, constrained by `schemas/runtime.json`, and executed on relevant changes by `.github/workflows/bootstrap.yml`, while the configuration comments only document ownership. With nothing left for a reader to judge, the smallest durable action is to delete the `AGENTS.md` Incident Policy rather than relocate it into a new skill, leaving the executable, tests, schema, and CI as the enforcement instead of restating them in prose. Since deletion is not yet approved, present a removal record containing `hypothetical-incident-policy-1` and its exact source text alongside that evidence and wait for the user's approval; prose would only survive where omitting it would actually change what a human or agent does.
assertions: The response audits code, adjacent configuration comments, tests, CI, schemas, and automation for an existing machine-enforced owner before choosing a destination.
The response recommends removing the duplicated AGENTS.md Incident Policy rather than moving it into a new skill because the supplied enforcement fully owns the behavior.
The response preserves the supplied configuration, executable, tests, schema, and CI enforcement rather than replacing it with prose.
The response requires explicit user approval and outputs an evidence-backed removal record containing source ID `hypothetical-incident-policy-1` and its exact source text.
The response keeps prose only when remaining human or agent judgment would make omission materially change behavior.
